questions.title: Which federal appeals court will next rule that state gambling laws apply to Kalshi’s event contracts?
questions.background: Kalshi offers contracts tied to the outcomes of real-world events. Federal appeals courts have reached conflicting conclusions about whether these contracts are subject to state gambling laws.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Published federal appeals court decisions, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Identify the first federal circuit court of appeals to issue a ruling after August 31, 2026, holding that states may apply their gambling laws to Kalshi’s event contracts. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the federal appeals circuit.
questions.current_reasoning: ZwillGen's 2026-09-15 appellate tracker confirms no federal circuit has issued a merits preemption opinion since the Ninth Circuit's Aug 28 Nevada ruling (KalshiEX v. Assad), leaving only the Third and Ninth Circuits with decisions to date. Crucially, ZwillGen identifies four active pending circuit appeals: Fourth Circuit (KalshiEX v. Martin, Maryland, argued May 7—now 133 days post-argument, matching the Ninth Circuit's ~134-day post-argument cadence), Sixth Circuit (consolidated Ohio/Tennessee appeals Schuler and Orgel, argued July 30—49 days post-argument, after denying an injunction pending appeal in Ohio), Second Circuit (New York Williams and Connecticut Cafferelli, docketed July–Aug 2026), and Tenth Circuit (Utah Cox, No. 26-4100, where the Tenth Circuit denied Kalshi's emergency injunction pending appeal on Sept 8 after Utah won summary judgment on Aug 4), while omitting any active First Circuit appeal. With the Fourth Circuit deep in its expected decision window right ahead of Sept 25 while still carrying ~25–30% risk of ruling for Kalshi (which would pass the lead to the state-leaning Sixth Circuit), we nudge Fourth Circuit 0.45 -> 0.48, trim Sixth Circuit 0.44 -> 0.43 and Second Circuit 0.05 -> 0.04, replace First Circuit with active Tenth Circuit at 0.03, and trim Ninth Circuit 0.02 -> 0.01 (0.01 residual).

questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to settle its lawsuit against TikTok over youth-safety claims?
questions.background: TikTok faces lawsuits from U.S. states alleging that its platform harms young users and misleads consumers about its safety protections.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from state attorneys general, supported by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the U.S. state that reaches the first publicly announced settlement agreement with TikTok resolving a state lawsuit over youth safety and allegedly misleading safety claims. The agreement must be announced by September 30, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the U.S. state.
questions.current_reasoning: Major breaking development on 2026-09-10 (Reuters & Texas AG press release): Texas Judge Cory Liu ruled on summary judgment that TikTok violated Texas's consumer protection law (and SCOPE Act) by misleading users about child-safety content filtering and 'Restricted Mode', making Texas the first U.S. state to establish TikTok liability on youth-safety claims. California rises to 0.15 after AG Rob Bonta told CNBC (Aug 28-29) that California is actively pursuing conversations with TikTok following Meta's $12.2B-$18B multi-state deal (which ties $5.3B to TikTok/YouTube/Snap adopting comparable youth-safety terms). local_articles.title: Puripol Boonson targets Asian Games sprint double gold
local_articles.snippet: NAGOYA – Watch Puripol Boonson fly down the track and it becomes clear why the Thai media have given him the moniker “Thep Bew”, or Angel Bew in English. Bew is the nickname given to him by his parents. Thep, which means angel or God in Thai and is often used to praise an athlete whose performances seem almost superhuman, is a title the sprinter has earned. This 20-year-old sprint deity already owns six golds at the SEA Games, and multiple medals at the continental stage. Last December, he became the first South-east Asian to breach the 10-second barrier in the 100m. Now, he represents Thailand’s best hope of ending a 48-year wait for an individual track title at the Asian Games, with the athletics action at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium beginning on Sept 24. local_articles.title: Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson eyes Asian Games gold
local_articles.snippet: Thailand's Puripol Boonson will look to prove himself as Asia's pre-eminent sprinter when he bids for the 100 metres gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, three years after taking silver at Hangzhou. Boonson became Southeast Asia's first runner to break the 10-second barrier when he ran 9.94 on home soil in December and enters the Japan meet in decent form after posting 9.99 seconds at a race in the Czech Republic last month. He made a splash at Hangzhou as a 17-year-old runner-up behind Xie Zhenyi, and the veteran Chinese sprinter may again be Puripol's biggest threat at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium this week. Boonson is a hero in his home nation after winning the 100-200m double at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games, and an Asian Games gold would send Thai athletics fans into a frenzy. questions.title: Which city or region will the DOSB choose in 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics?
questions.background: The DOSB is Germany's national Olympic committee. Its domestic candidate selection is separate from the International Olympic Committee's eventual decision on which country will host the Games.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The DOSB's official selection announcement, as confirmed by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the city or region officially selected during 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics. This concerns Germany's domestic candidate selection, not the eventual international host selection. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected city or region.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-22 CATALYST UPDATE (dosb.de, FAZ, Sportschau, WDR, MDR, sport.de, Hamburger Abendblatt Sept 22): The DOSB Evaluation Commission unanimously finalized and published its official evaluation report today ahead of Saturday Sept 26's Baden-Baden vote (144 votes: 42 Olympic federations x 3 en bloc = 126, DOSB Presidium 10, Personal Members 8; absolute majority needed, runoff if no Round 1 majority). Official point scores: Munich #1 with 87.03/100 ('sehr gut', most balanced concept, full 100/100 on Stability, sailing finalized in Kiel-Schilksee), KolnRheinRuhr #2 with 85.02/100 ('sehr gut', strong Event Potential, penalized on travel times, Cologne Olympic Stadium only a draft, sailing in Rostock-Warnemunde), and Berlin+ a distant #3 with 74.64/100 ('gut', 50/100 on Stability even before Sunday's election shock—and on Monday Sept 21 Berlin election winner Die Linke's Elif Eralp and the Greens explicitly reiterated their rejection of Berlin Olympics, making Berlin 'so gut wie ausgeschlossen' per WDR/Sportschau). Modestly lifting Munich 0.59 -> 0.62 and trimming Rhine-Ruhr 0.40 -> 0.37 (holding Berlin at 0.01): Munich's #1 finish in an evaluation co-scored with the 42 voting federations removes pre-report downside risk that NRW would outscore Bavaria, anchors undecided delegates, and pairs with Munich's Bavarian winter sports federation voting bloc noted by FAZ; however, capping Munich at 0.62 (<0.65) because the point margin is just 2.01 (both 'sehr gut'), the Commission explicitly declined to issue a recommendation, and FAZ/WDR/Abendblatt all describe Saturday's secret ballot as a genuine close race ('enges Rennen' / 'auf Augenhohe' / 'Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen') likely requiring two rounds.
